sources.entry: Woodpecker CI | Simple yet powerful CI/CD engine

summary.one_liner: Woodpecker is a self-hostable CI/CD engine that runs pipelines with an extensible plugin system.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Woodpecker as a simple but powerful CI/CD engine with extensibility through plugins. It can be installed in several ways (the README points to separate installation instructions) and uses SQLite as its default database. The README states it needs roughly 100 MB of RAM for the server and 30 MB for the agent when idle. Plugins can be browsed on a plugin overview website, which lists both core-team and community-maintained plugins. The README also notes that Codeberg uses Woodpecker as its main CI/CD engine. Documentation and translation resources are linked externally.
use_cases: run automated builds and tests for git repositories
replace a hosted CI service with a self-managed one
how_to_run: See the Installation Instructions referenced in the README (no commands included in the README itself)
stack: Go (implied by the agent and server components; not named in README)
notable: Plugin ecosystem with a browsable overview website, mixing core-team and community plugins
Low idle resource footprint stated as about 100 MB RAM server and 30 MB agent
Used as the main CI/CD engine at Codeberg
caveats: README does not include install commands; it refers to external installation instructions
Documentation and plugin overview live on external sites not included in the README
